transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I guess I’m here because things at work have been getting difficult, and I’m not sure I’m explaining it the right way. For over a year now, I’ve been trying to get someone to take seriously that the new ticket rotation and these security audits seem like they’re being used to build a paper trail against me. 

Management keeps showing me logs and telling me it’s just policy, and I understand how that sounds, but it doesn’t feel that simple from my side. I just thought maybe talking to someone could help me sort out how to handle it.
Do you believe for certain that your management is deliberately trying to build a case against you?

I don’t want to sound unreasonable, and I know they keep showing me logs and saying it’s just policy… but yes, I do think that’s what’s happening. Maybe “certain” is a strong word, but from my side it really looks like the ticket rotation and those audits are being used to create a paper trail on me. It’s been going on long enough that it’s hard for me to see it as just coincidence.
Have you ever heard voices when no one else was there?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve never had a voice talking to me when nobody was there, if that’s what you mean. Sometimes I replay conversations in my head, especially after work stuff, but that’s just thinking, I think… right?
Do you think it’s possible you might be mistaken about management trying to build a case against you?

I mean… I suppose anything is possible. I’m trying to be fair about it, and I know they keep saying it’s just policy and showing me the logs.

But honestly, from where I’m sitting, it’s been over a year of the ticket rotation and these security audits lining up in a way that really feels like they’re building a paper trail against me. I don’t want to seem stubborn, Doctor, but it’s hard for me to believe I’m just imagining the pattern.
Have you had the feeling that other people can read your thoughts?

No… I don’t think so. I’ve never really felt like people could literally read my thoughts. Sometimes I worry people are judging me or interpreting what I do at work, but that’s different, I think. I don’t have the sense that my thoughts are being broadcast or anything like that.
Have you ever felt that someone was controlling your actions?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I make my own decisions and move how I want to move. I’ve never felt like someone was… physically or mentally taking over my actions, if that’s what you mean. Sometimes I feel pressured at work, but that’s normal pressure, not control. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Outside of work, do you often feel that other people are trying to harm you or plot against you?

Not really outside of work, no. I mean, I don’t walk around thinking strangers are after me or anything like that.

It’s mostly this situation at work… the ticket rotation and the security audits. For over a year it’s felt like they’re being used to build a paper trail against me, even though management keeps saying it’s just policy and showing me logs. I know that probably sounds… maybe intense, but that’s the main place I feel it.
Has there been any moment when you were fully convinced that management was deliberately building a case against you?

Yes… I think there have been times where I felt pretty sure about it. I don’t want to sound unreasonable, but after this went on for so long—the ticket rotation changing, the security audits, and then management telling me it was all just policy while showing me logs—it started to feel like they were putting together a paper trail on me.

That’s really why I’m here, I guess. I’ve been trying for over a year to get someone to take it seriously, because to me it doesn’t feel random or routine. But I know how that might come across, so I’m trying to explain it carefully.
Have you ever seen things that other people could not see?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t seen people or things that weren’t there, at least not that I’m aware of. Sometimes I might misread something out of the corner of my eye, like anyone does, but nothing where I’d say I saw something other people couldn’t see. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Before this situation at work began, did you generally tend to distrust other people’s motives?

I don’t think so, not generally. I mean, I’ve always tried to be careful with people, especially at work, but I wouldn’t say I went around assuming people had bad motives.

Before this started, I think I mostly took things at face value. At least… that’s how I remember it. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Did this start after a specific stressful event at work?

Yes, I think so. It seemed to start around when the hybrid schedule changed and the after-hours ticket rotation changed. I don’t want to make too much of it, but that was the point where I began noticing things felt different.

That would’ve been about a year and two months ago now, roughly. Does that sound like the kind of specific event you mean?
Since this started, has your ability to manage your daily life or do your job gotten much worse?

Not much worse overall, I don’t think. I mean, outside of the issue with the ticket rotation and the audits, I still keep the house in order, pay the bills, help my wife with things, and do the technical parts of my job.

Nobody’s told me my work is sloppy or that I’m disorganized, at least not in that way. So… I don’t want to sound defensive, but I think I’m still functioning pretty well. Does that answer it?
Since this began, have you had a period where you felt unusually energetic and needed much less sleep than usual?

No, I don’t think so. I’ve had some nights where I slept poorly, but not like I felt unusually energetic or didn’t need sleep.

If anything, I’d say I still need my normal rest. I’m not aware of a period like that. Is that what you mean?
Has this belief that management is building a case against you been there continuously for at least three months?

Yes… I’d say it’s been there since around those schedule and ticket rotation changes, so about a year and two months now.

I don’t mean it’s been at the same intensity every single day, but the concern itself hasn’t really gone away. That’s probably the honest answer.
Since this began, have you become much less emotionally expressive or less interested in being around other people?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I may be a little more careful about who I talk to at work, but I wouldn’t say I’ve become emotionally flat or stopped wanting to be around people.

At home I’m still myself, I think. My wife might say I’m preoccupied sometimes, but not… not withdrawn in that way. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Is there any part of this situation at work that you believe involves something clearly impossible or supernatural?

No, I wouldn’t say supernatural or impossible. I’m not talking about, you know, mind reading or cameras in the walls or anything like that.

It’s more… ordinary workplace stuff, I guess. The ticket rotation, the security audits, the logs they keep showing me—management says it’s just policy, but I feel like those things are being used to build a paper trail against me. That’s the part I’ve been trying to get taken seriously.

So no, not impossible. It’s just hard to prove, I suppose.
